name: FT4232HL-Reel
title: FT4232H: USB 2.0 high-speed to quad UART / dual MPSSE bridge, LQFP-64, QFN-64, VQFN-56
summary: A single-chip bridge from USB 2.0 high speed (480 Mbit/s) to four serial channels. All four work as UARTs up to 12 Mbaud or as 8-bit bit-bang ports; channels A and B also hold an MPSSE engine for JTAG, SPI, I2C and other synchronous buses at up to 30 Mbit/s. It runs from 3.3 V with an on-chip 1.8 V core regulator and a 12 MHz crystal, uses an optional 93C46/56/66 EEPROM for its USB descriptors and options, and works with FTDI's VCP and D2XX drivers. It comes as the FT4232HL (LQFP-64), FT4232HQ (QFN-64) and FT4232H-56Q (VQFN-56), rated -40 °C to 85 °C.
key_figures: 2.0 high speed 480 Mbit/s, full speed 12 Mbit/s
4 UART / bit-bang; 2 of them also MPSSE
2 kbyte TX + 2 kbyte RX per channel
VCCIO 2.97 V to 3.63 V; VCORE 1.62 V to 1.98 V (on-chip LDO)
70 mA typ operating, 500 µA typ suspend
30 mA typ, 60 mA max at 480 MHz
±2 kV HBM, ±200 V MM, ±500 V CDM

notes: The base numbers are FT4232HL, FT4232HQ and FT4232H-56Q, with a -Reel or -Tray packing suffix. All packages are lead free and RoHS compliant, and every function is available in each.

circuits.title: RS232 port on channel A
circuits.description: A complete bus-powered board with channel A wired to a MAX3241 line transceiver and a DB9 connector. All eight UART lines of channel A go to the transceiver's logic side (TXD, RTS# and DTR# into its drivers, RXD, CTS#, DSR#, DCD# and RI# from its receivers), and the line side goes to the DB9. Its charge pump uses four 100 nF capacitors, with a fifth bypassing VCC; PWREN# drives pin 23 and SUSPEND# drives SHDN, so the transceiver sleeps with the USB bus. The supply side is the bus-powered arrangement with these differences: 100 nF at VREGOUT, 30 pF crystal capacitors, a 93LC46B with its own 100 nF bypass, a 100 kΩ pull-down on RESET# beside the 1 kΩ pull-up, and the USB shield tied straight to ground. Channels B, C and D repeat the same way when needed.

circuits.title: USB bus-powered configuration
circuits.description: Power comes from the USB cable. An external LDO turns VBUS into 3.3 V for VREGIN, VCCIO, VPLL and VPHY; the on-chip regulator then makes 1.8 V at VREGOUT, held up by 3.3 µF, which feeds the three VCORE pins. RESET# is pulled to 3.3 V through 1 kΩ. The 3.3 V rail feeds VCCIO, and reaches VPLL and VPHY each through its own inductor with a 4.7 µF and a 100 nF capacitor. Three 100 nF capacitors bypass the 1.8 V core pins and four the 3.3 V I/O pins. REF has its 12 kΩ to ground, a 12 MHz crystal with two 27 pF caps runs the oscillator, and TEST and AGND go to ground. A 93C46 EEPROM holds the configuration: CS on EECS, SCL on EECLK, D on EEDATA, and Q back to EEDATA through 2.2 kΩ; EECS, EECLK and Q have 10 kΩ pull-ups, ORG is tied high. The USB shield returns to ground through a link marked 0?. All four channels are left free for the application.

circuits.description: Power comes from the USB cable through two external LDOs: one makes 3.3 V for VCCIO, VPLL and VPHY, the other 1.8 V for the VCORE pins, each with 100 nF at input and output. The on-chip regulator is not used. RESET# is pulled to 3.3 V through 1 kΩ. The 3.3 V rail feeds VCCIO, and reaches VPLL and VPHY each through its own inductor with a 4.7 µF and a 100 nF capacitor. Three 100 nF capacitors bypass the 1.8 V core pins and four the 3.3 V I/O pins. REF has its 12 kΩ to ground, a 12 MHz crystal with two 27 pF caps runs the oscillator, and TEST and AGND go to ground. A 93C46 EEPROM holds the configuration: CS on EECS, SCL on EECLK, D on EEDATA, and Q back to EEDATA through 2.2 kΩ; EECS, EECLK and Q have 10 kΩ pull-ups, ORG is tied high. The USB shield returns to ground through a link marked 0?. All four channels are left free for the application.

circuits.title: USB self-powered configuration
circuits.description: Power comes from an external supply on J2, brought to 3.3 V by an LDO; the on-chip regulator makes 1.8 V at VREGOUT (3.3 µF) for the VCORE pins. VBUS does not power anything: it drives a 4.7 kΩ / 10 kΩ divider whose midpoint pulls RESET# through 1 kΩ, so the chip stays in reset while no USB cable is present. The EEPROM has to be set for self-powered operation. The 3.3 V rail feeds VCCIO, and reaches VPLL and VPHY each through its own inductor with a 4.7 µF and a 100 nF capacitor. Three 100 nF capacitors bypass the 1.8 V core pins and four the 3.3 V I/O pins. REF has its 12 kΩ to ground, a 12 MHz crystal with two 27 pF caps runs the oscillator, and TEST and AGND go to ground. A 93C46 EEPROM holds the configuration: CS on EECS, SCL on EECLK, D on EEDATA, and Q back to EEDATA through 2.2 kΩ; EECS, EECLK and Q have 10 kΩ pull-ups, ORG is tied high. The USB shield returns to ground through a link marked 0?. All four channels are left free for the application.

circuits.title: Dual RS422 ports on channels A and C
circuits.description: Channels A and C run as TTL UARTs, each feeding two full-duplex RS485 transceivers that make RS422 levels on a DB9: one carries TXD and RXD, the other RTS# and CTS#. Each receiving pair has a 120 Ω termination across it at the connector. SUSPEND# drives every driver enable and PWREN# every active-low receiver enable, so the transceivers drop to low quiescent current while the USB bus is suspended. Channels B and D can be added the same way.

circuits.title: Dual RS485 ports on channels A and C
circuits.description: Channels A and C each drive a half-duplex RS485 transceiver on a two-wire bus. TXD feeds the driver input and RXD takes the receiver output; the channel's TXDEN pin (ADBUS7, CDBUS7, set to TXDEN in the EEPROM) turns the driver on only while a character goes out, and PWREN# holds the active-low receiver enable, so the receiver is off in USB suspend. A 120 Ω resistor in series with a link sits across each bus pair, to be fitted when the board is at one end of the cable. The transmitting node hears its own data; software can discard it, or an OR gate (an HC32 or similar) of the receiver output with TXDEN in front of RXD removes it in hardware.

notes: Of U1, only the channel A and C pins and PWREN# are part of this circuit.
The channel C connector pins are named DM_B and DP_B.

circuits.title: 12 MHz crystal oscillator
circuits.description: A 12 MHz parallel-cut crystal across OSCI and OSCO, each side loaded to ground by 27 pF. The crystal tolerance is ±0.003 %; 27 pF suits many crystals, but the load capacitance the crystal's manufacturer recommends is the better choice. A 12 MHz CMOS-output oscillator into OSCI, with OSCO open, can replace the crystal.

circuits.title: Transmit and receive LEDs for four channels
circuits.description: A 74HC595 shift register listens to the EEPROM bus and lights a red LED for transmit and a green LED for receive on each channel, each through 330 Ω from a register output (QA to QH in the order ATx, ARx, BTx, BRx, CTx, CRx, DTx, DRx). EECLK clocks EEDATA into the register while EECS is low, so the EEPROM ignores those bits; the rising edge of EECS then latches them to the outputs. PWREN# drives the active-low output enable, which a 10 kΩ resistor pulls up to VIO. The LEDs also flicker whenever the EEPROM itself is read, as in enumeration.

operation.text: Four independent serial channels sit behind one USB 2.0 high-speed (480 Mbit/s) device port; full speed (12 Mbit/s) also works. Channels A and B each contain an MPSSE as well as a UART, so they can run JTAG, SPI, I2C, bit-bang or a custom synchronous protocol; channels C and D are UART or bit-bang only. The chip handles the whole USB protocol itself, so no USB firmware is written for it. Each channel has its own 2 kbyte transmit and 2 kbyte receive buffer and its own baud rate generator.

Under software control the device runs as 2 MPSSE plus 2 UART channels, 1 MPSSE plus 3 UARTs, or four UARTs, and any UART channel can switch to bit-bang for extra I/O. With one or both MPSSEs in use, channels C and D still pick UART or bit-bang freely. Each channel's mode is independent of the others.

After reset all four channels are asynchronous UARTs. The application changes a channel's mode with the D2XX FT_SetBitMode command; a reset puts every channel back to UART, so modes are set again after one. The EEPROM does not choose the mode, except that it turns the RI# pin into TXDEN for RS485 use.

The UART is the FT232B style: 7 or 8 data bits, 1 or 2 stop bits, odd, even, mark, space or no parity, and hardware (RTS/CTS, DTR/DSR) or X-On/X-Off flow control. Rates run from 183 baud to 12 Mbaud, except that 7, 9, 10 and 11 Mbaud cannot be produced. RS232 speed is limited by the external level shifter.
Each channel derives an x16 or x10 UART clock from a 120 MHz reference with a 14-bit prescaler and 4 fraction bits, so the divisor can be a whole number plus a fraction.

With TXDEN selected in the EEPROM, the eighth line of a UART channel goes active only while a character is being sent, which is the enable an RS485 driver needs. The node then also receives its own transmission.

The Multi-Protocol Synchronous Serial Engine, on channels A and B only, is driven by commands sent in the data stream and sustains up to 30 Mbit/s. Its clock, CLKOUT, is 30 MHz at most and can be divided down. Set Bit Bang Mode with value 2 turns it on and value 0 resets the device. One use is loading an SRAM FPGA from the PC over USB while the other MPSSE handles another serial bus.

An MPSSE can handshake its clock with a returned clock from the target, as ARM cores use: it raises TCK and waits for RTCK to come back on GPIOL3 before changing its data output, which changes on the falling edge of TCK. Adaptive clocking is off by default.

Any channel can run as 8 bits of I/O, each pin separately an input or an output. Bytes written to the channel appear on the output pins at the rate of the baud rate generator; with no new data the pins keep their last value. Set Bit Bang Mode with value 1 selects it.

The pins are sampled only when a byte is written: each write first reads the pins, then drives the new byte, so the data read back runs one byte behind. Starting from 0xFF, writing 0x55 then 0xAA returns 0xFF, 0x55; writing a third byte (repeating 0xAA) returns 0xFF, 0x55, 0xAA. Output only proceeds while the transmit FIFO has room for the readings. Set Bit Bang Mode with value 4 selects it.
The driver sends a part-filled packet back to the PC when the latency timer runs out: 16 ms by default, adjustable from 0 ms to 256 ms. At 0 ms a packet goes out every high-speed microframe.

The I/O cells, the PHY and its PLL run from 3.3 V; the core runs from 1.8 V. The on-chip LDO makes that 1.8 V from 3.3 V at VREGIN and gives at most 150 mA; it has no internal connection to the core, so the board wires VREGOUT to the VCORE pins, with at least 3.3 µF on it. A capacitor on VREGIN is recommended. VPHY cannot be fed from VBUS directly; it needs a 3.3 V regulator, and LC filters on VPHY and VPLL are recommended. The I/O pins tolerate 5 V, except the USB PHY pins.

Bus-powered, a regulator turns VBUS into 3.3 V for VCCIO, VPLL, VPHY and VREGIN, and the core comes from the internal LDO or from a second external 1.8 V regulator. Self-powered, an external supply feeds the same rails and VBUS only pulls RESET# through a divider, keeping the chip in reset with no USB host; the EEPROM must then declare self power. The power configurations apply to every package.
An internal power-on reset starts the chip at power-up. RESET# lets external logic reset it and is tied to VCCIO when not used.

The UTMI PHY serialises and deserialises the USB data at high and full speed, recovers clock and data, does bit stuffing and SYNC/EOP handling, manages suspend, resume and wake-up, and clocks the whole device from a 12 MHz crystal and an on-chip PLL (12 MHz to 480 MHz). REF needs 12 kΩ to ground. The oscillator input wants 12 MHz within ±30 ppm with under 150 ps of cycle-to-cycle jitter.

Without an EEPROM, or with a blank one, the device enumerates as four serial ports with VID 0403, PID 6011, its default description and power value, and no serial number. A 93C46, 93C56 or 93C66 (16-bit wide, able to clock at 1 Mbit/s with VCC from 3.0 V to 3.6 V, such as a 93LC46B) lets an OEM set VID, PID, serial number, strings and the power descriptor, plus I/O pull-downs at power-off, remote wake-up, I/O drive strength and the RI#/TXDEN choice. It can be programmed in circuit over USB with FT_PROG, so a blank part can be fitted and programmed at test. FTDI gives out blocks of PIDs free to customers who lack their own VID.

With remote wake-up enabled in the EEPROM, pulling RI# low resumes a suspended host, in about 20 ms. Pull-ups on the interface lines must stay powered in suspend, and no path may partly power the peripheral. In suspend the peripheral may draw up to 2.5 mA when remote wake-up is on and no more than 500 µA when it is off. With the suspend pull-downs enabled the device does not wake from suspend.
Output drive strength is set in the EEPROM to 4, 8, 12 or 16 mA, and a slow slew rate can be chosen as well.

operation.topic: LED indication through the EEPROM bus
operation.text: In normal running EECS stays low, which keeps the EEPROM idle, while EECLK (1.56 µs) clocks status bits out on EEDATA and a high pulse on EECS ends each frame. A 74HC595 on those three lines latches the bits on the rising edge of EECS and can drive a transmit and a receive LED for each channel.

The device complies with USB 2.0 and holds USB-IF test ID 40720024. Rise and fall times of the USB signals also depend on layout, external parts and transient protection; they can be trimmed by a setting in the EEPROM or by passive parts on the lines.

The device appears to a host as virtual COM ports through FTDI's royalty-free VCP driver, or is reached directly through the D2XX driver and its DLL. Both cover Windows (98 to 10, CE 4.2 to 6.0, XP Embedded) and Linux 2.4 and later; VCP also covers Mac OS 8/9 and OS X, and D2XX Android (J2xx). Dedicated DLLs exist for JTAG, SPI and I2C over USB.
The parts are MSL 3: 168 hours of floor life out of the bag at 30 °C and 60 % RH, after which they are baked at +125 °C for up to 17 hours.
The QFN-64 and VQFN-56 have a central pad on the underside that has to be soldered to system ground; on the VQFN-56 it is 5.90 mm by 5.90 mm and carries the die ground.
The top carries four lines: the FTDI logo, the date code and revision (YYWW-A on the 64-pin parts, YYWW-C on the FT4232H-56Q), the wafer lot number, and the part number.
